title: the test suite leaks daemonised intentd processes: 27 orphans, 249 minutes of CPU, none answering
body:
**TWENTY-SEVEN LEAKED `intentd` PROCESSES WERE RUNNING, NONE OF THEM ANSWERING, HAVING BURNED 249 MINUTES OF CPU.** Found 2026-09-08 while diagnosing an unrelated report from Utilz. Cleared by hv's order; evidence at `scratchpad/leaked-daemons.txt`.

**NOT ONE WAS THE MACHINE DAEMON.** `intent daemon status` read `ok: no intentd is answering; commands run in-process` throughout, and no pidfile or endpoint existed under `~/.intent` or `/tmp`. **All 27 were orphans serving nothing**, `PPID 1`, 26 debug builds and 1 release, all from `native/rust/target/`.

**TWO POPULATIONS, SEPARATED BY CPU TIME:**

    ~9 HOT    19 to 40 minutes of CPU EACH, spinning for hours
    ~18 INERT 0:00.02 -- started, did nothing, never exited

**THEY ARRIVE IN BURSTS OF 3-4 WITHIN ONE SECOND**, repeatedly: 12:48, 12:49, 12:50, 12:51 (eight), 13:46, 14:18, 14:20. The shape inside a burst is 3 at second N and 1 at N+1.

**THE FD LAYOUT NAMES THE MECHANISM.** Each holds BOTH ENDS of its own socketpair, plus a duplicate:

    fd 6u  unix 0x349e..aa -> 0x6d63..68
    fd 7u  unix 0x6d63..68 -> 0x349e..aa      <- the other end of its OWN pair
    fd 8u  unix 0x349e..aa -> 0x6d63..68      <- duplicate of fd 6

**A correct daemonise is fork -> setsid -> fork -> parents exit.** Here the intermediates survive, each holding descriptors it should have closed -- which is exactly the 3-inert-plus-1-hot signature, once per start.

**THE SOURCE IS THE TEST SUITE.** Eight test files spawn a real `intentd`: `daemon_lifecycle`, `daemon_run_execs`, `daemon_and_local_agree`, `mcp_bridge_restart`, `cli_routing`, `dual_path_conformance`, `edit_and_browse_reach_one_model`, `graphql_escape_hatch`. **The burst timestamps coincide with test runs, and the processes outlive the run that started them.**

**THEY DO HONOUR `SIGTERM` -- IT TAKES ABOUT FOUR SECONDS.** All 27 exited cleanly on TERM and Intent's store was healthy afterwards (`doctor` runs, 71 threads, 262 issues). **So graceful cleanup is available and nothing invokes it.** An immediate recount after TERM showed 27 still alive and was a RACE, not a refusal -- worth stating, because the obvious next step from that reading is `SIGKILL`, which would leave the SQLite WAL hot.

**WHAT THEY DID NOT DO, AND THIS MATTERS BECAUSE IT WAS ABOUT TO BE FILED AS A CROSS-PROJECT DEFECT:** they held **only Intent's own tree**. `lsof` on four of them, including every hot one, returns ZERO handles on `Utilz`, `Lamplight` or `Conflab`; the release process holds `cwd = Devel/prj/Intent` and `intent/.cache/intent.db-shm`, Intent's own database. **These daemons were not writing another project's `.intentfiles`.**

**AND THE ARCHITECTURE IS NOT AT FAULT.** `intent daemon --help` describes a MACHINE-LEVEL daemon, and every verb carries `--daemon` as opt-in -- *ask a running intentd instead of this process*. The default is in-process and local, so ordinary CLI work in an unrelated project touches no daemon at all. **The defect is the leak, not the design.**

**RELATED FROM THE OTHER SIDE:** `0281` records that the macOS app's `IntentCLI` spawns children Foundation makes group leaders, with nothing signalling the group -- a leak of the same family in a different runtime. **Two spawn paths in one estate, neither cleaning up after itself.**
